notes: FICTIONAL equal-weight complete cohort, not real participants or recovered target data. No excluded-study quantitative results used. Sources were independently retrieved through Europe PMC. SCIENTIFIC CHOICE: joint age/sex/BMI model followed by correlated measured aggregate SBP/DBP, keeping both outcomes on each row. (1) ASSOCIATION ANCHOR: Gnatiuc et al., Hypertension 2017, DOI 10.1161/HYPERTENSIONAHA.116.08791, PMC5344187 version 2, Results/Discussion and Table 1: 111,911 Mexico City adults aged 35-89, 1998-2004, no known chronic disease and no BP-lowering medication; manual seated BP after 5-min rest, mean of three over about 6 min, measured anthropometry. Models adjusted for age, sex, residential district, education, smoking, physical activity and alcohol. Text reports approximate 3/2 mmHg higher SBP/DBP per 4.5 kg/m2 BMI (not exact coefficients or confidence limits). Derived generator slopes are 3/4.5 and 2/4.5 mmHg per unit BMI, hence 3.33/2.22 per 5. These are transported conditional association parameters, NOT established age/sex-only coefficients for treated Brazilian adults. Constant slopes across ages/sexes, removal of the source's extra adjustment variables, extrapolation below 35, and applicability despite disease/treatment inclusion are substantial assumptions. No causal interpretation. Do not treat printed sample slopes as those input parameters. (2) MARGINAL BRAZILIAN ANCHORS: Brant et al., JAHA 2014, DOI 10.1161/JAHA.114.001279, PMC4338719 Table 1 and Methods, 1,535 ELSA-Brasil participants from Minas Gerais; civil servants age 35-74 selected for successful PAT testing, mean age 52 SD9, female44%, BMI26.8 SD4.6, SBP122 SD17, DBP78 SD11, hypertension treatment28%, diabetes16%. Automatic Omron765CP, mean second/third of three readings after 5-min seated rest. Use BMI26.8 and measured BP122/78 at age52 as approximate location anchors, NOT a marginal fit to an all-adult or weighted survey population. SDs16.2/10.4 at52 are approximate residual scale choices motivated by subtracting modest age/sex/BMI-explained variance from source marginal17/11; source does not report these residual SDs or the relevant covariance decomposition. Male-female differences4.5 mmHg, BMI sex-specific SD4.2/4.9, all age-BMI means, shifted-lognormal BMI form, support14-60 and shift12 are explicit assumptions anchored loosely to this scale and Mexico's larger female BMI dispersion. Source-age reference mean BMI is approximately26.8 under44%female at52. Mexican age-specific BP table informs mean age shapes for35-79, interpreted at BMI26.8 after reference recentering. Choosing to apply marginal source age shapes to conditional BP means, interpolating group centers37,45,55,65,75, estimating younger shapes20/30 and endpoint79, and age-specific residual scale multipliers are assumptions. ELSA clinical sample supplies larger SDs than untreated Mexico; source SDs were not silently averaged. (3) JOINT DEPENDENCE: Badaruddoza et al., J Adv Res 2015 (online2014), DOI10.1016/j.jare.2014.04.002, PMC4563590 Table2, parental generation30.5-60.7 years, n954 (439men/515women), Ramdasia community north-west Punjab, 2008-2011, healthy and no medication for2weeks; pregnancy excluded. Mean of two consecutive BP readings following AHA recommendations. Published Pearson correlations, upper triangle men/lower women, are recorded in dependence_evidence. For each sex derive residual rho=(rSD-rSX inv(RXX) rDX')/sqrt((1-rSX inv(RXX) rSX')*(1-rDX inv(RXX) rDX')), X=(age,BMI). This gives approximately0.642 men and0.724 women. This is algebra on rounded correlations under linear adjustment, not a reported adjusted correlation, genetic correlation, or uncertainty interval. Holding those correlations across20-79, transferring to Brazil and treated/diseased adults, assigning Gaussian conditional errors and stated SDs are major assumptions. Pooled downstream residual correlation is emergent, not forced to either source value. Rows are independent; family structure in source is not recreated. (4) CONTEXT ONLY: Chor et al., PLoS One2015 DOI10.1371/journal.pone.0127382, PMC4478044 Methods/Tables1-2, ELSA-Brasil15,103 civil servants35-74, female54.4%; 35.8%hypertension,76.8%of hypertensives treated; automated mean last two of three1minute-apart readings. Confirms treatment inclusion matters; not used to simulate or restrict hypertension/treatment. Shares ELSA participants with Brant and is not independent replication. (5) HETEROGENEITY CHECK: Chen et al., J Hum Hypertens2015 DOI10.1038/jhh.2014.129, PMC4537884 Methods/Results, Pengzhou China53,578 not taking antihypertensives, adjusted age, education,income,smoking,alcohol,fruit,sedentary time,season; mean two digital readings, third if needed. Reports6.7/3.6 mmHg per5 BMI, stronger than Mexico. Not averaged or used as numeric model anchor because population adiposity, management and measurement differ. DEMOGRAPHY: decade shares and age-specific female probabilities in spec are modeling assumptions, not extracted target weights. They create a broad Brazilian-context adult scenario; no evidence identifies the peso_lab complete-case age/sex distribution. Extrapolation to20-34 and75-79 especially weak. No nationally representative assertion. ELIGIBILITY: directly generate the already-eligible complete-case adult distribution, no HbA1c, disease, treatment or hypertension restriction; no pregnancy model/variable; reported pregnancy exclusion and retention of unknown/inapplicable pregnancy are taken as preconditions rather than verifiable generated fields. Positive laboratory weights and selection are absorbed into equal-weight transport; neither lab selection nor actual peso_lab values are recovered. MEASUREMENT: output BP represents one fictional final-interview aggregate, not long-term usual pressure; baseline timing and unknown released final-reading aggregation remain unresolved. No claim the unknown aggregation is two or three readings; no correction for its effect on SD or correlation is identified. Rounding1decimal is an implementation assumption, not claimed survey instrument precision. Resample entire SBP/DBP error pairs until SBP70-260, DBP40-150 and pulse pressure>=15; these are modeling guardrails, not asserted dictionary limits. Such truncation slightly changes slopes/correlations. BMI rounded2decimals, integer baseline ages exposed as numeric. ANALYSES: primary linear-age OLS and Pearson residual correlation as specified in intended_analysis; flexible-age sensitivity is also computed from generated-only records. No finite-sample orthogonalization/raking/selection to force appealing results. Reproduce via generate(None, model_spec, seed); diagnostic execution only checks generated records and not reference or source agreement.
